_comment: Node-filling baseline on Ant-v4 alone: the plain `base` experiment (default physics, reward and termination)
for 9M steps on 188 random seeds = 188 runs, one per core on a 192-core node (4 cores reserved).
Companion of trillium_humanoid_base_9m.json (same seeds, same layout, Humanoid-v4); together they give a
homogeneous-node utilisation profile per env (see scripts/profiling/README.md). Profiling only: the seeds are not
matched to any other config. Hyperparameters are the paper's Ant-v4 settings, as in every other Trillium config; same gamma/beta1/
normalisation flags, videos every 3M steps and at the end, model snapshots every 1M steps.
Seeds: 188 distinct values drawn once (numpy default_rng(20261103).choice(100000, 188, replace=False)) and
written here so the job is reproducible.
At the ~459 steps/s measured for Ant-v4 on a full shared node (18M profiles), 9M is ~5.4 h per run;
submit with --time=09:00:00 and TIME_LIMIT=8.5 (a slow run checkpoints and exits before the walltime) and its own
RESULTS_DIR so the run folders and the profiling monitor folder of this job stay apart from the other jobs':
The utilisation monitor is on by default (MONITOR=1): profiling CSVs land in $RESULTS_DIR/monitor_<jobid>;
scripts/profiling/README.md has the resume and plotting commands.

experiments.name: base
experiments._: default physics, default reward/termination, Ant-v4 only
